implementation_notes: The standard library ships the whole pattern: queue.Queue (or the reentrant, unbounded SimpleQueue) is the thread-safe multi-producer/multi-consumer buffer with put/get, task_done/join completion tracking and shutdown() to wind it down; asyncio.Queue is the coroutine twin with await put/get and its own shutdown path; a bare collections.deque with append/popleft is the lock-free choice when the drain runs in the same thread as the enqueue. What replaces the classic structure is the queue class plus one drain point - the classic hand-written queue is justified only for a fixed ring buffer or coalescing the stdlib does not provide.
pitfalls: asyncio.Queue is not thread-safe and queue.Queue is not loop-aware: bridging the two needs loop.call_soon_threadsafe, and mixing them silently races.
A blocking get() with no timeout can park a worker forever on shutdown - use shutdown() (3.13+), a timeout or a sentinel, and call task_done() for everything you got or join() hangs.
An unbounded queue.Queue hides the back-pressure problem: producers outrun the drain and memory grows, so set maxsize and decide what a full queue means.
